summary: The video presents a landscape photography workflow that emphasizes creating depth through controlled lighting and careful composition, then executing a zone-based, history-driven post-processing approach. The speaker argues for a single light source, exclusion of peripheral distractions, and a three-dimensional eye path driven by blacks and light. He demonstrates layered compositions using drones and telephoto lenses to build depth, discusses how fog, mist, and weather shape transitions, and contrasts wide-angle versus telephoto perspectives. The processing segment guides viewers through RAW adjustments, zone-based editing in Photoshop, and color grading with blue/gold filters, highlight grading, and selective color to separate flowers and mountains. Throughout, the instructor advocates a painting-with-history mindset—painting with the history panel as a stand-in for traditional layers—to rapidly refine tonal balance, color consistency, and focal emphasis.

sections.title: Lighting philosophy and scene exclusion
sections.description: The speaker advocates using one light source where possible, avoiding conflicting lighting, and shaping the scene so the eye is drawn along a clear light path. He emphasizes landscape as a puzzle of many elements where exclusion of distractions is crucial to cohesion.

sections.title: Layered composition, spacing, and transitions
sections.description: Discussion of building depth via layers (mountains, trees, foreground) and tactically spacing subjects to avoid overlap. Emphasizes keeping periphery free of bright distractions and using blacks to create depth.

sections.title: Lenses, framing, and drone-based layering
sections.description: Explains using telephoto from a drone to create layered framing, with attention to spacing so key subjects don’t touch and to avoid peripheral distractions. Highlights how wide-angle framing naturally creates big-to-small transitions and leading-line dynamics.

sections.title: RAW-to-Photoshop: zone-based editing and dynamic range
sections.description: Covers converting to Photoshop after RAW processing, assigning zones for localized edits, and using whites to recover sky while preserving foreground detail. Demonstrates blue/gold filter and highlight grading to begin color balance and mood, then uses the history brush to paint changes in.

sections.title: Advanced color grading: selective color and color harmony
sections.description: Shows sophisticated color grading, including selective color adjustments to separate floral tones, balancing hues via color-wheel-based adjustments, and ensuring color coherence between sky, foliage, and mountains.
